title: The complement of a closed point in a separated irreducible positive-dimensional scheme over a field is not proper

standard_prerequisites.name: The image of a proper scheme under a separated morphism is closed
standard_prerequisites.use: Contradicts non-closedness of U to show U is not proper over the base field.

core_obligations: Use irreducibility of X to see that U = X setminus {x} is not closed in X, so the open immersion U -> X is not proper (proof lines 9195-9196).
Apply the closedness of images of proper schemes, together with separatedness of X, to conclude that U -> Spec(k) is not proper either (proof lines 9197-9198).
proof_roadmap: Show the open immersion is not closed, hence not proper.
Transfer non-properness to the structural morphism using separatedness.
difficulty_reason: The lemma proves that for a separated irreducible scheme X over a field of dimension greater than zero, the open subscheme obtained by deleting a closed point is not proper over k. The proof observes that irreducibility makes U = X setminus {x} fail to be closed in X, hence the open immersion U -> X is not a closed immersion and therefore not proper; since X is separated, the closedness criterion for images of proper schemes then shows that U -> Spec(k) cannot be proper either (proof lines 9195-9198). H2: the argument is short but genuinely two-step, and the separatedness hypothesis is used exactly in the second step.
